title: fix: omit Windows null timestamps in OneDrive and Outlook

files.patch:
@@ -1,3 +1,9 @@
+## [1.12.4]
+
+### Fixes
+
+- **OneDrive no longer aborts when a file time is the Windows null filetime.** Microsoft Graph uses `1601-01-01 00:00:00` for recovered or unsaved files. `datetime.timestamp()` goes through the platform C `mktime`: on Windows that raises `OSError` and stops the ingest, and on other platforms it returns a large negative epoch that is not a real file time. Outlook wrote the same Graph value through `.timestamp()` after labeling it UTC, so the null was stored as a modification time there too. `safe_timestamp()` treats that exact instant as missing, and also returns `None` when `timestamp()` raises `OSError`, `OverflowError`, or `ValueError`. OneDrive and Outlook leave `date_created` and `date_modified` unset. Ordinary timestamps are unchanged.
+

+
+
+# Windows FILETIME epoch. Microsoft Graph uses this instant as a null timestamp
+# on recovered or unsaved files (issue #517).
+_WINDOWS_NULL_FILETIME = (1601, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0)
+
+
+def safe_timestamp(dt: Optional[datetime]) -> Optional[str]:
+    """Epoch seconds as a string, or None when the value is not a real file time.
+
+    ``datetime.timestamp()`` raises OSError or OverflowError for 1601-01-01 on
+    platforms whose C mktime rejects it, and otherwise returns a large negative
+    epoch. Dates the platform cannot convert raise ValueError. Indexers omit
+    all of those instead of aborting the file.
+    """
+    if dt is None:
+        return None
+    if (
+        dt.year,
+        dt.month,
+        dt.day,
+        dt.hour,
+        dt.minute,
+        dt.second,
+        dt.microsecond,
+    ) == _WINDOWS_NULL_FILETIME:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return str(dt.timestamp())
+    except (OSError, OverflowError, ValueError):
+        return None
